title: Advanced Visual Information-Graphics Marine (SSgt to Sgt), NMOS (4512, 4541, 4571, 4591), DIR COMM
raw_text:
5. MOS 4513, Advanced Visual Information-Graphics Marine (SSgt to Sgt), NMOS
(4512, 4541, 4571, 4591), DIR COMM

    a. Summary. Advanced Visual Information-Graphics (AVI-G) Marines are
the 45XX occupational field enlisted visual information specialists,
specifically trained and experienced in graphic arts and design disciplines.
AVI-G Marines serve as the Service’s advanced storytellers through their
extensive education and experience in visual communication disciplines. AVI-
G Marines use multidisciplinary techniques and elements to create master-
level visual communication products that present information with strong
visual impact and that can be used in multiple formats across a wide range of
communication spaces. They are responsible for conducting technical training
and education in the graphic art and design disciplines to Fleet Marine Force
and Supporting Establishment Communication Strategy and Operations
(COMMSTRAT) Marines and will develop training plans that ensure individual
and collective Training and Readiness task compliance. AVI-G Marines will
directly supervise the implementation of the 45XX indoctrination and managed-
on-the job training (MOJT) programs related to 4512 technical skillsets and
provide 1st-level validation of skills competency. AVI-G Marines will mentor
junior Marines in the technical disciplines of graphic art and design and
provide technical counsel to senior COMMSTRAT staff non-commissioned officers
and officers regarding visual communication theory, application, and
capabilities.

       b.   Prerequisites.   Must possess PMOS 4512, 4541, 4571, or 4591.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Digital Multimedia Course (A18T4Z2), Defense
Information School, Ft Meade, MD.

        (2) Successful completion of a minimum of 21 semester hours (or
equivalent quarter hours) of a graphic arts and design curriculum from an
accredited university or professional civilian graphic arts school. Submit
transcript to 45XX OccFld sponsor to certify completion of specialized
graphic art and design training with correlating courses in fundamentals of
communication design, principles and elements of graphic design, design
conceptualization, design processes, fundamentals of color theory,
typographic design, multimedia storytelling, motion graphics and animation,
immersive arts, and marketing and branding. Include copies of course
descriptions from university or civilian trade school catalog.

        (3) The Director of Communication (DIRCOMM), Headquarters Marine
Corps, is the certifying authority for additional MOS (AMOS) 4513 for those
Marines that meet requirements (1) and (2). Waivers for these requirements
will not routinely be considered, however DIRCOMM is the awarding authority
for AMOS 4513, and as such may waive requirements as deemed necessary.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to the
COMMSTRAT Training and Readiness Manual (NAVMC 3500.9C).

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) General and Operations Managers 11-1021.

            (2) Public Relations and Fundraising Managers 11-2031.




                                         3-298                        Enclosure (1)
 3132                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



            (3) Training and Development Managers 11-3131.

            (4) Project Management Specialists 13-1082.

            (5) Training and Development Specialists 13-1151.

            (6) Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists 13-1161.

            (7) Archivists 25-4011.

            (8) Art Directors 27-1011.

            (9) Producers and Directors 27-2012.

            (10) News Analysts, Reporters, and Journalists 27-3023.

            (11) Public Relations Specialists 27-3031.

            (12) Editors 27-3041.

            (13) Writers and Authors 27-3043.

            (14) Media and Communication Workers, All Other 27-3099.

            (15) Film and Video Editors 27-4032.

            (16) Production, Planning, and Expediting Clerks 43-5061.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1)   Combat Graphics Specialist, 4512.

            (2) Combat Photographer, 4541.

            (3) Combat Videographer, 4571.
common_text: (COMMSTRAT) 1. Introduction. In addition to the Communication Strategy and Operations (COMMSTRAT) Officer, the Visual Information Officer and the COMMSTRAT Planner, the 45XX occupational field (OccFld) is comprised of the following primary military occupational specialties (MOS) Combat Graphics Specialist, Combat Photographer, Combat Videographer and COMMSTRAT Chief. The 45XX OccFld is also comprised of the following additional military occupational specialties (AMOS) Recruiting Station Marketing and Communication Marine, Advanced Visual Information-Graphics Marine, Advanced Visual Information- Photojournalism Marine and Advanced Visual Information-Motion Media Marine. Regardless of specialty, 45XX OccFld Marines are employed in both the operating forces and supporting establishment. The OccFld’s mission is to advise commanders and staffs on communication strategy matters, to communicate with internal, domestic, and international audiences through engagement, acquire and disseminate written and visual information products to support planning and operations, develop and synchronize communication plans by conducting research, planning, implementation, and evaluation in order to build understanding, credibility, and trust with audiences critical to mission success. The COMMSTRAT OccFld conducts a variety of tasks in support of operational and institutional objectives, to include acquiring, editing, and producing written, photo, video, graphic and illustration products in electronic and print formats, and communicating with internal, domestic, and international audiences through a variety of means, such as the traditional news media, social and emerging media, community engagement, and support to key leader engagements. Through the official release of truthful and timely information, the 45XX OccFld puts Marine Corps operations, policies, programs, and activities in context, and counters misinformation, disinformation and adversary propaganda. Marines entering the 45XX OccFld will receive the MOS 4500 (Basic Communication Strategy and Operations Marine) upon successful completion of Phase I (A1824Q2) of the PMOS-granting pipeline at the Defense Information School (DINFOS), Ft Meade, MD. Upon graduating phase I, 4500 Basic Marines will stay at DINFOS to complete their intended MOS (IMOS) producing phase II course.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
